correctness.rationale: The normalized block overlaps give \(U^*V=(1-r/p)I+(r/p)S\) and hence \(U^*PQPU=I-\tau\Delta\), where \(\tau=r(p-r)/p^2\). Fourier–Floquet fibers are rank-one projectors with squared overlap \(\lambda(\theta)=1-4\tau\sin^2(\theta/2)\), yielding imaginary commutator eigenvalues \(\pm i\sqrt{\lambda(1-\lambda)}\) and zero. Continuous matrix multipliers establish both full and Fredholm essential spectra, while almost-everywhere fiber ranks establish the kernel. Parseval and a Gaussian rescaling give the moment-by-moment sharp coefficient. The standalone checker passed 135 finite Bloch spectral instances, 276 phase-threshold comparisons, and twelve high-iteration asymptotic tests; no finite experiment was treated as a proof.

originality.rationale: The reviewed contribution is the parameter-specific, complete bilateral staggered-grid commutator spectrum with its sharp \(1/8\) transition, exact heat-step representation, and localized moment asymptotics. General two-projection decomposition and abstract alternating-projection convergence theorems are prior ingredients, not stated explicit results about these grids. Direct mathematical record and literature comparisons revealed no dominating result for the same equal-width staggered lattice geometry. Equivalences and residual specialized-literature risks remain explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: The unshifted or shifted alignment of blockwise averaging is a basic concrete setting for alternating projections and repeated signal reconciliation. The sharp \(\tau=1/8\) commutator transition, full essential spectral interval, heat-step equivalence and moment-by-moment sharp decay classify nontrivial geometric and dynamical behavior across every width and stagger. The moment law identifies which localized inputs can converge rapidly despite norm-nonconvergence and supports quantitative iteration estimates; it is not an arbitrary isolated small-dimensional parameter.
